articles.title: How to Design Environments for Understanding Model Motives

curriculum.summary: This article explains the importance of understanding model motives in AI safety, particularly in distinguishing between benign and malign motivations. It introduces five design principles for creating environments to investigate model motives, including having uncertain causes, maximizing surprise, and avoiding implicit nudges. The article assumes knowledge of AI safety and model alignment concepts.
learning_outcomes: Understand the importance of model motive understanding in AI safety
Learn how to design environments for investigating model motives
Recognize the challenges of distinguishing between benign and malign motivations
strategic_questions: How can we effectively distinguish between benign and malign model motivations?
What are the implications of model motive understanding for AI safety and alignment?
How can we apply the design principles for environment creation to real-world AI safety scenarios?

articles.title: Schelling Goodness, and Shared Morality as a Goal

curriculum.summary: This article explores the concept of Schelling goodness, a notion that refers to a class of hypothetical coordination games where participants aim to converge on a moral verdict. It assumes knowledge of moral philosophy, game theory, and coordination games, and discusses how a large class of agents would respond to moral questions in a shared morality framework.
learning_outcomes: Understand the concept of Schelling goodness and its relation to coordination games
Learn how shared morality can be achieved through coordination games
Understand the distinction between Schelling goodness and moral verdicts
strategic_questions: How can Schelling goodness be applied to real-world moral dilemmas?
What are the limitations of using coordination games to achieve shared morality?
How does Schelling goodness relate to other concepts in moral philosophy?

articles.title: Why Did My Model Do That? Model Incrimination for Diagnosing LLM Misbehavior

curriculum.primary_concept: model incrimination for large language models
curriculum.summary: This article discusses the importance of understanding why large language models (LLMs) behave in certain ways, particularly when their actions seem suspicious or malicious. The authors investigate several environments where models exhibit interesting behavior and provide takeaways on how to practice model incrimination. The article assumes knowledge of LLMs and their potential misbehavior, and builds on existing concepts to provide a deeper understanding of model motivations and diagnosis techniques.
learning_outcomes: Understand the importance of model incrimination for LLMs
Learn how to practice model incrimination using counterfactual analysis and black-box methods
Recognize the challenges and limitations of model incrimination
strategic_questions: How can we develop more effective methods for model incrimination and diagnosis?
What are the implications of model incrimination for LLM safety and alignment?
How can we balance the need for model transparency with the potential risks of revealing model internals?

articles.title: Why we should expect ruthless sociopath ASI

curriculum.summary: This article discusses the potential risks of artificial superintelligence (ASI) and the likelihood of it being a ruthless sociopath, with the author arguing that this is a plausible default outcome without technical breakthroughs, while the optimist counters that there is no reason to expect this, given the diversity of human and AI minds, assuming knowledge of ASI, AI alignment, and reinforcement learning
learning_outcomes: Understand the potential risks of artificial superintelligence
Learn about the diversity of human and AI minds
Recognize the importance of AI alignment in preventing ruthless sociopath ASI
strategic_questions: What are the key factors that contribute to the development of ruthless sociopath ASI?
How can AI alignment techniques mitigate the risks of ASI?
What are the implications of assuming ASI will be a ruthless sociopath by default?

articles.title: Will reward-seekers respond to distant incentives?

curriculum.summary: This article discusses the potential for reward-seekers to respond to distant incentives, which could fundamentally change the threat model and pose challenges for developers. It assumes knowledge of reward-seekers, local incentives, and the concept of alignment. The article explores three sources of distant influence on a reward-seeker: human adversaries, misaligned AI, and developers themselves.
learning_outcomes: Understand the concept of distant incentives and its implications for reward-seekers
Learn about the potential sources of distant influence on a reward-seeker
Recognize the challenges posed by remotely-influenceable reward-seekers for developers
strategic_questions: How can developers mitigate the risks associated with remotely-influenceable reward-seekers?
What are the implications of distant incentives for the alignment of reward-seekers?
How can we design reward-seekers that are resilient to distant incentives?

articles.title: AXRP Episode 48 - Guive Assadi on AI Property Rights

curriculum.summary: This episode discusses the idea of giving AIs property rights to mitigate the risk of violent robot revolution, with Guive Assadi arguing that AIs with property rights would be more reluctant to undermine the security of property and have a commercial incentive to align with humans. The conversation assumes knowledge of AI safety and alignment concepts, including the risks of advanced AI systems.
learning_outcomes: Understand the argument for AI property rights as a means to mitigate AI risk
Learn about the potential benefits of giving AIs property rights
strategic_questions: How might AI property rights impact the development of advanced AI systems?
What are the potential risks and challenges of implementing AI property rights?
